observations.behavior: Reduced token and character limits for generated briefing content.
observations.posthog_connection: These limits constrain the length of AI-generated summaries shown to users; tighter limits reduce token usage and response time.

observations.behavior: Revised voice and formatting instructions for the AI briefing, including a shorter headline and more concise paragraphs.
observations.code_quote: Voice: write like a teammate who sends a quick Slack message. Casual and short. Use everyday words and contractions ("it's", "there's", "you're"). Sentence case, no hype. The person reads the whole text in about 10 seconds, so give only the gist of each item. Less is better: when a sentence works without a word, cut the word. Cut filler such as "it looks like", "you may want to", "this is a" or "worth a look". Do not use formal words such as "currently", "additionally", "regarding", "requires", "pending" or "impacted". Do not use technical detail from the summary, such as error names, file names, metric names or numbers the person does not need to decide. Do not explain what a product or tool does. Use the words the person sees in PostHog. Never an em dash or an en dash; use a comma or a new sentence. Never quote customer text, never name customers or people, and never name a time of day: the page greets the person itself and the text stays up for hours.
observations.posthog_connection: Changes the AI's stylistic and structural behavior, potentially improving readability and reducing filler, but no runtime behavior is demonstrated.

observations.behavior: Revised signal examples and headline examples, and removed imperative commands from the AI's output.
observations.code_quote: - `signal`: the short fact that makes it matter, at most {{ max_signal_chars }} characters. Examples: "Needs your call", "P1, fix ready", "P0, no owner".
